CHOICE: 3

CONFIDENCE: 3

I checked Solution 3's counterexample directly. Its eight generators are exactly the minimal lattice points of the Newton polyhedron of $(x^2,y^3,z^7)$, so the ideal is integrally closed. The point $xy^2z^6$ lies in $\overline{I^2}$ because $\tfrac12+\tfrac23+\tfrac67=\tfrac{85}{42}\ge 2$, and no pair of generators divides it, so $xy^2z^6\notin I^2$. That shows a non-normal integrally closed height-3 ideal with 8 generators exists, so $N\le 7$. Solution 1's citation looks unreliable, and Solution 2's claim that every 4-generator case is normal is only sketched, not proved. I could not verify from memory that every such ideal with at most 7 generators is normal, so the value 7 rests on an unconfirmed theorem. My confidence is low for that reason.
